summary:
There's genuinely nothing to report today: every metric in the feed is a bare current-value snapshot with no 1d/7d/30d deltas populated, which means there isn't yet enough history to say what "changed" in any measurable sense. No hiring data, no compute-utilization or power/buildout figures, and no percent changes on stock price, volume, or 8-K counts for any of the eighteen companies tracked here — Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Nvidia, Broadcom, AMD, TSMC, ASML, Arm, Oracle, Dell, Supermicro, CoreWeave, Digital Realty, Equinix, Vertiv, and Eaton. Every one of them shows zero 8-K filings today, which is unremarkable on its own — 8-K counts are lumpy and a single zero-day tells you nothing either way.

The open-source signals (commit activity on PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, llama.cpp, TensorRT-LLM, DeepSpeed) are similarly just point-in-time counts — PyTorch at 100 commits and vLLM at 73 in the last 24 hours stand out as the most active repos in absolute terms, but without a baseline to compare against, there's no way to say whether that's elevated, normal, or depressed activity.

In short: no basis yet for calling synchronized moves across companies, no cross-metric divergences worth flagging, and no individual mover worth highlighting — this is a data-collection snapshot, not a signal day. Once enough history accumulates to populate the 1d/7d/30d deltas, this dashboard should start showing whether hiring, spend, and filing activity are moving together or diverging across the group. Worth checking back once trailing windows fill in rather than reading anything into today's raw levels.
